security_audit.summary: The main confirmed issues are in recalc.py, which writes a persistent LibreOffice macro and invokes LibreOffice on user-provided workbooks. The hardcoded URL is an XML namespace, and the SKILL.md backtick and reconnaissance findings are Markdown documentation false positives. No prompt injection attempt was found in the reviewed skill files.

remediation.suggestion: Use a temporary LibreOffice user profile for recalculation, or remove the macro after use with clear user consent.
Restrict input paths to the workspace, keep shell execution disabled, and document that untrusted workbooks need sandboxing.
Add file-size, sheet, row, column, and timeout limits before scanning workbook cells for formula errors.

semantic_findings.title: Persistent LibreOffice Macro Installation
semantic_findings.description: The script installs a RecalculateAndSave Basic macro into the LibreOffice user profile before processing workbooks. This persists outside the workspace and affects later LibreOffice runs.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The macro path, Module1.xba write, and RecalculateAndSave macro body are visible in recalc.py. This confirms persistent application-profile modification.

semantic_findings.title: Unbounded Workbook Cell Scanning
semantic_findings.description: The recalculation script scans all cells across all worksheets twice after opening the workbook. A crafted or very large workbook could cause local resource exhaustion.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The code iterates every row and cell with no sheet, row, column, or file-size limit. The risk is denial of service rather than code execution.

content.value_statement: Spreadsheet work often needs formulas, formatting, and validation to stay reliable. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structured Excel workflows.
actual_capabilities: Explains how to create Excel workbooks with formulas, formatting, and worksheet structure.
Guides edits to existing workbooks while preserving templates, formulas, and styles.
Uses pandas workflows for reading, summarizing, and exporting spreadsheet data.
Uses openpyxl workflows for formulas, formatting, sheets, rows, and columns.
Provides a LibreOffice-based recalculation script that checks formulas for common Excel errors.
Gives financial model formatting standards for colors, numbers, assumptions, and source notes.
limitations: Formula recalculation requires LibreOffice and local script execution.
The recalculation script modifies the local LibreOffice user profile to install a macro.
Very large workbooks may be slow because the script scans all cells for errors.
It provides workflow guidance and helper code, not a full spreadsheet application.

best_practices: Keep assumptions in separate cells and reference them from formulas.
Preserve existing workbook conventions when editing templates.
Recalculate and inspect formula errors before delivering a workbook.
anti_patterns: Do not hardcode calculated values when formulas should update dynamically.
Do not save a workbook after loading it with calculated values only.
Do not run recalculation on untrusted workbooks without local security controls.

faq.question: What spreadsheet formats does this skill target?
faq.answer: It focuses on Excel workbooks, including xlsx and xlsm, plus CSV and TSV data workflows.

faq.question: Can it preserve formulas in existing files?
faq.answer: Yes. It recommends openpyxl workflows that preserve formulas and existing workbook structure during edits.

faq.question: Does it calculate Excel formulas by itself?
faq.answer: No. It uses LibreOffice through the included recalc.py script to recalculate workbook formulas.

faq.question: Is LibreOffice required?
faq.answer: LibreOffice is required only for formula recalculation and formula error checking.

faq.question: Can it help with financial models?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes formatting, color, assumption, and source documentation standards for financial models.

faq.question: What security review result matters most?
faq.answer: The helper script executes LibreOffice and writes a macro into the local LibreOffice profile, so review before use.
